title: Map incident root causes to PRD scope and acceptance contracts
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Purpose: Convert recurring incident findings into deterministic PRD scope decisions so that product requirements, rollout gating, and acceptance criteria explicitly prevent or mitigate prioritized failure modes.

Background: Multiple incidents in Q3/Q4 showed gaps between post-incident remediation items and what product PRDs require to avoid recurrence. Engineering fixes land in ad-hoc repos and runbooks; product requirements are often vague about operational acceptance and verification. This ticket establishes a repeatable mapping from incident origin categories (e.g., kernel regressions, cache staleness, autoscale cold-starts, cross-region routing) to explicit PRD scope items and measurable acceptance contracts (SLO + verification harness + runbook acceptance).
acceptance_criteria: A canonical taxonomy of incident origin categories is documented and accepted by Eng/Oncall/PM/Design (doc link in Links).

For each high-priority incident category (initial scope: kernel regressions, KV cache stalls, coldstart autoscale), PRD template fields are defined that capture: user-visible impact, allowed degradation budget, required telemetry signals, rollback criteria, and operator runbook steps.
PRD template changes are merged into the Product PRD checklist and visible in Confluence and the PRD starter template PR (see Links).
Three pilot PRDs (one per incident category) adopt the new template and show concrete acceptance criteria with corresponding synthetic tests or dashboards wired to CI/CD smoke suites.
A gated rollout process is defined: every rollout that touches serving runtime or routing must include an incident-origin risk assessment and a signed acceptance checklist by PM + owning ENG + SRE.
Owners are assigned for maintaining the incident-to-PRD mapping document and for quarterly reviews; responsibility is visible in the PRD metadata in Confluence.
steps: Draft incident taxonomy and map to example PRD clauses (owner: Marcus) — due 2025-11-18.
Workshop with SRE and Runtime leads to validate mapping and acceptance signals — scheduled 2025-11-21.
Update PRD starter template and open Confluence PR for review — due 2025-11-28.
Implement pilot PRDs for three features and add synthetic verification to CI — due 2025-12-08.
Run acceptance review with stakeholders and sign off on process — due 2025-12-12.
notes: 2025-11-05: Kickoff meeting — agreed on initial scope: kernel regressions, KV cache stalls, autoscale coldstarts. Action: Marcus to draft taxonomy.
2025-11-12: Received SRE feedback: telemetry signals for cache stalls need a 5-minute aggregation window to avoid noisy flapping; added to ACs.
2025-11-19: Design review — noted UI requirement to surface the 'incident-origin' field in PRD metadata so downstream Console teams can surface it in rollout dashboards.

2025-11-25: Engineering raised a tradeoff: adding strict rollback gates increases release cycle time for small fixes. Decided: make gates mandatory for runtime-impacting changes and optional with justification for others.
2025-12-02: Pilot PRD #1 (cache eviction policy change) created and linked; proof-of-concept dashboard created in Grafana to validate acceptance signals.
2025-12-09: Legal requested a short clause for regulated customers describing notification obligations for degradations; added to PRD template as optional section.
impact_summary: By codifying incident-origin awareness into PRDs we expect a measurable reduction in regression-driven incidents (target: 40% reduction in repeat incidents for covered categories within 6 months) and faster operational recovery due to clearer runbooks and built-in verification. This will also standardize the operator checklist used in rollouts and make rollback criteria unambiguous for SREs and PMs.
